database_summary: This SQLite database contains a mix of sales and marketing facts, user/event logs, cryptocurrency members/transactions/prices, and several vegetable (veg_) datasets. Tables include time-series facts (weekly_sales, cleaned_weekly_sales, bitcoin_transactions, bitcoin_prices, veg_txn_df, veg_whsle_df, interest_metrics), event logs (shopping_cart_events), user/member/reference dimensions (shopping_cart_users, bitcoin_members, interest_map, customer_regions, shopping_cart_page_hierarchy, shopping_cart_event_identifier, shopping_cart_campaign_identifier), and small lookup/category tables (veg_cat, veg_loss_rate_df). Some tables represent cleaned/derived versions (cleaned_weekly_sales). Several tables share identifier-like columns (cookie_id, member_id, page_id, item_code) that enable joins but may multiply rows when joining event-like tables to aggregated facts.

accepted.name: cleaned_weekly_sales_metrics
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  week_date_formatted,
  week_date,
  calendar_year,
  month_number,
  week_number,
  region,
  platform,
  segment,
  customer_type,
  SUM(transactions) AS transactions,
  SUM(sales) AS sales,
  AVG(avg_transaction) AS avg_transaction
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
GROUP BY
  week_date_formatted,
  week_date,
  calendar_year,
  month_number,
  week_number,
  region,
  platform,
  segment,
  customer_type
accepted.description: Aggregated weekly sales measures at the cleaned week x region x platform x segment x customer_type grain. Useful for trend analysis, cohort comparisons, and as a base for further time-window calculations. | Use for: Time series of sales/transactions by region/platform/segment/customer_type; Compare average transaction value across segments or customer types; Monthly or weekly aggregations derived from cleaned weekly data

accepted.name: weekly_sales_raw_period
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  week_date AS week_date,
  region AS region,
  platform AS platform,
  segment AS segment,
  customer_type AS customer_type,
  transactions AS transactions,
  sales AS sales
FROM weekly_sales
accepted.description: Normalizes week_date text from weekly_sales into a pass-through view exposing the raw textual week_date and original attributes. Use this to parse/convert week_date externally or join to cleaned_weekly_sales while preserving original source columns. | Use for: Cleaning/parsing week_date formats; Join raw weekly_sales to other tables after normalization; Inspecting source-level differences vs cleaned_weekly_sales

accepted.name: shopping_events_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.visit_id AS visit_id,
  e.cookie_id AS cookie_id,
  e.page_id AS page_id,
  p.page_name AS page_name,
  p.product_category AS product_category,
  p.product_id AS product_id,
  e.event_type AS event_type,
  i.event_name AS event_name,
  e.sequence_number AS sequence_number,
  e.event_time AS event_time
FROM shopping_cart_events e
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p ON e.page_id = p.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier i ON e.event_type = i.event_type
accepted.description: Denormalized shopping cart events with page and event name lookups. One row per event (visit_id x sequence_number). Useful for funnel, page-level, and event sequencing analyses. | Use for: Session funnels and pathing (page sequences per visit); Counts of event types by page or product category; Time-to-event or time-between-events per visit

accepted.name: shopping_users_latest_cookie
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  user_id AS user_id,
  cookie_id AS cookie_id,
  start_date AS start_date,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY start_date DESC) AS user_cookie_rank
FROM shopping_cart_users
accepted.description: Latest cookie assignment per user_id from shopping_cart_users based on start_date. One row per user_id with a rank so downstream queries can filter to the latest mapping. | Use for: Joining latest cookie to events for user-level analysis; Identify cookie churn or multiple cookies per user over time

accepted.name: bitcoin_txn_member_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  member_id AS member_id,
  ticker AS ticker,
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  txn_type AS txn_type,
  SUM(quantity) AS quantity,
  AVG(percentage_fee) AS percentage_fee,
  COUNT(txn_id) AS txn_count
FROM bitcoin_transactions
GROUP BY
  member_id,
  ticker,
  txn_date,
  txn_type
accepted.description: Aggregate bitcoin transactions per member_id x ticker x txn_date. Useful for member-level activity summaries, joining to member demographics, or computing rolling metrics. | Use for: Member activity (volumes and counts) by date and ticker; Fee analysis by member or transaction type; Joining aggregated transactions to bitcoin_prices for P&L

accepted.name: bitcoin_prices_timeseries
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticker AS ticker,
  market_date AS market_date,
  price AS price,
  open AS open,
  high AS high,
  low AS low,
  volume AS volume,
  change AS change
FROM bitcoin_prices
accepted.description: Pass-through view of bitcoin_prices exposing price measures by ticker and market_date for time-series joins. Useful before parsing market_date to native date type in downstream queries. | Use for: Price history and volatility calculations; Join prices to transactions by ticker and date; Compute daily returns or moving averages after parsing dates

accepted.name: veg_item_master
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.item_code AS item_code,
  c.item_name AS item_name,
  c.category_code AS category_code,
  c.category_name AS category_name,
  l."loss_rate_%" AS "loss_rate_%"
FROM veg_cat c
LEFT JOIN veg_loss_rate_df l ON c.item_code = l.item_code
accepted.description: Master item-level reference for vegetable datasets combining category and loss-rate information. One row per item_code with category and loss rate where available. Useful for enriching transactional veg data. | Use for: Enrich veg transactions with category and loss rate; Aggregate sales by veg category or analyze loss impacts

accepted.name: customer_transactions_by_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  SUM(txn_amount) AS txn_amount,
  COUNT(*) AS txn_count
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
accepted.description: Aggregated customer transactions by customer_id and txn_date with sums and counts. Useful for customer-level behavior and joining to customer_nodes or regions. | Use for: Customer daily spend and frequency; Joining transactions to customer_nodes or regions for segmentation

accepted.name: customer_nodes_active
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  region_id AS region_id,
  node_id AS node_id,
  start_date AS start_date,
  end_date AS end_date
FROM customer_nodes
WHERE end_date IS NULL
accepted.description: Customer node assignments where the assignment is currently active (no end_date) or ongoing. One row per customer_id x node_id assignment. Useful to find current node placements for customers. | Use for: Current node assignment lookup for customers; Joining customer current nodes to transaction history
